body_markdown:
Adalo has helped many non-technical founders and small teams build native mobile apps through its visual drag-and-drop interface. However, as app-building technology evolves, teams increasingly want options that combine AI-powered development with production-ready infrastructure.[Floot](https://floot.com/) offers a full-stack approach with managed hosting, databases, authentication, and mobile app workflows.


Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , Floot works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. This guide examines seven Adalo alternatives through the lens of full-stack app development, helping founders, freelancers, and small business owners find the right fit for their projects.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Reduced learning curve** : AI-powered app building reduces the need to master visual builders or learn to code, allowing teams to describe apps in natural language to generate functional applications.
- **Backend infrastructure matters** : Managed databases, authentication, scheduled tasks, and transactional email determine whether an app can handle real users beyond demonstration purposes, and Floot provides[comprehensive backend services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) without requiring separate database or authentication infrastructure, although some production features require additional configuration or paid plans.
- **Code ownership and export** : Floot users own their code own their code and data on every plan, with full TypeScript/React project ZIP export available on paid plans. However, self-hosting may require replacing Floot-managed services and migrating hosted files.
- **Pricing models vary** : Per-app pricing, usage-based credits, and unlimited-app subscriptions create different cost structures, and[Floot offers unlimited projects](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/billing-credits-and-plans) on paid subscription plans while hosting remains usage-billed.
- **Mobile app approaches differ** : Some platforms generate native builds, others wrap web apps in installable shells, and[Floot converts web apps](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) to native iOS/Android shells without requiring separate mobile development.


## **Understanding Conversational App Development with AI Assistants**


The traditional no-code approach requires learning a platform's specific interface, understanding its component library, and mastering its workflow logic. AI-powered app builders take a different approach: teams describe what they want in natural language, and the AI generates the application.


This shift matters for several reasons. Describing changes in conversation moves faster than clicking through visual editors. Conversational building reduces the need to learn a visual editor, though apps still require testing and iteration. AI assistants can use earlier parts of conversations and apply that context to new features. Platforms using Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors let teams build through supported AI assistants using existing AI subscriptions, although available building capabilities depend on the connected client's permissions.


For non-technical founders building MVPs, this conversational approach often proves more intuitive than traditional visual builders.


## **No-Code and Low-Code Platforms: A Broad Overview**


Before diving into specific alternatives, it helps to understand the spectrum of available options. Visual builders use drag-and-drop interfaces with pre-built components, including platforms like Adalo, Bubble, and FlutterFlow. AI-first builders accept natural language input to generate applications, including platforms like Lovable and Bolt.new. Development environments with AI assistance provide full coding environments enhanced by AI tools, such as Replit and Cursor. Floot takes a connector-based approach, letting supported AI assistants handle development while it provides managed full-stack infrastructure.


Each approach suits different skill levels and project requirements. Visual builders work well for those comfortable learning a new interface. AI-first builders serve users who prefer describing their app in plain language. Development environments with AI assistance bridge the gap for those with some technical background who want speed without sacrificing flexibility.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development while Floot provides managed infrastructure, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


Floot also offers an optional in-app AI agent for builders who prefer working inside its editor. Through supported AI workflows, teams can build applications conversationally while Floot manages hosting, database services, authentication, and deployment.


### **Key Capabilities for App Builders**


- **MCP connector for AI assistants** : Build through supported Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT workflows using existing AI subscriptions. Available actions depend on client permissions.
- **Managed Postgres database** : Full relational database included without manual setup, with resource usage covered by Floot's hosting billing.
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without setting up separate OAuth apps.
- **Transactional email and push notifications** : Floot includes transactional email and push notifications. Sending emails to customers requires a verified sending domain on a paid plan, while native push requires connecting the relevant app-store account.
- **Scheduled tasks** : Run scheduled backend jobs for reports, data syncing, and maintenance on published apps with a paid plan.
- **File storage with CDN** : Store and serve images, documents, and assets with content delivery.
- **Payments and hosting** : Build payment-enabled applications through supported integrations and deploy them using[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , with live Stripe payments available on Pro and Power. A Stripe account is required, and Floot charges 1% per payment on Pro and 0% on Power, in addition to Stripe processing fees.


### **Why Floot Leads for Full-Stack App Building**


Floot combines conversational development with the infrastructure needed to operate working applications. Rather than requiring non-technical founders to configure databases, authentication providers, and hosting separately, the platform supplies these services through a managed environment. Teams can create customer portals, internal tools, booking systems, and SaaS applications with real user accounts and saved data.


The[mobile app conversion feature](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) packages web apps in native iOS/Android shells without requiring a separate mobile codebase. Floot handles mobile builds and supports TestFlight and Google Play testing workflows. Store publishing still requires developer accounts, and final approval depends on the respective app stores. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, while Apple is supported on every plan.


Floot is particularly suitable for non-technical founders and operators who already use an AI assistant and want to turn their ideas into published applications. Its managed backend, flexible development workflows, and[supported integrations](https://floot.com/en/integrations) help teams move beyond prototypes without managing the underlying infrastructure themselves.


### **Pricing Structure**


Floot is **free to start** , with the following monthly plans and allowances listed in its[current pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) :


- **Free ($0/month)** : Up to 100 build actions/day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting credit at signup, and 2 mobile builds/month.
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 AI credits/month, $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds/month, unlimited projects, and custom domains.
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 AI credits/month, $25/month hosting allowance, unlimited mobile builds, unlimited projects, and custom domains.


Annual billing provides two months free. Hosting beyond the included allowance is usage-billed against hosting credit, with optional auto-reload.


Building through supported AI assistants uses existing AI subscriptions and Floot building actions. Separate Floot AI credits apply to features such as the optional Floot agent, image generation, and AI inside published apps.


Users own their code, data, and IP on every plan.[Database export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) is available on all plans, with full project ZIP download available on paid plans.


## **2. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual and AI-assisted app builder for web and native iOS/Android apps, with a large ecosystem of plugins and templates. Founded in 2012, Bubble reported 7.2 million apps launched by builders in its 2025 year-in-review and has built a substantial community of developers and agencies.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual workflow builder** : Create complex business logic through a graphical interface.
- **Plugin marketplace** : Access thousands of plugins for additional functionality.
- **Database and backend** : Built-in data storage with privacy rules and API access.
- **Responsive design** : Build web applications that adapt to different screen sizes.


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble provides power for building complex web applications through its visual workflow system. The platform offers extensive customization through its plugin ecosystem and template marketplace. Teams building data-driven web applications can leverage Bubble's built-in database and privacy controls.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble works well for teams building complex web applications who are willing to invest time learning the platform. The visual workflow system offers functionality for advanced use cases. Pricing uses workload units, which means costs vary depending on app usage patterns.


## **3. Lovable**


Lovable positions itself as a full-stack AI app builder with visual editing capabilities. The platform generates frontend and backend code from natural language prompts.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-powered generation** : Describe applications and receive generated code.
- **Visual refinement** : Edit generated applications through the preview toolbar, with some edits consuming AI credits.
- **Code export** : Sync projects through Git on all plans or download full project ZIP files on paid plans for continued development elsewhere.
- **Database options** : Use Lovable Cloud's managed Postgres database or connect to Supabase.


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable focuses on web applications and uses a credit-based pricing model. The platform provides both AI generation and visual editing tools for refining generated applications. Teams can export code for external development or continue building within the platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable targets founders building web MVPs who want AI generation with the option to refine visually. Teams should evaluate how credit consumption aligns with their iteration patterns, as complex projects may use credits quickly.


## **4. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new from StackBlitz is an AI-powered builder for web and mobile apps, using WebContainers for browser-based development and Expo for mobile projects. The platform runs a full Node.js environment directly in browsers.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Instant prototyping** : Generate working previews from prompts quickly.
- **WebContainers** : Full Node.js runtime in the browser without server setup.
- **Code export** : Download generated code to continue elsewhere.
- **Bolt Cloud** : Backend services including database and authentication.


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new prioritizes speed of initial generation for rapid experimentation with ideas. The platform runs applications directly in the browser using WebContainers technology. Teams can export generated code or deploy using Bolt Cloud services.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new serves teams that want to experiment with ideas rapidly before committing to a full build. For production deployment, teams can use Bolt Cloud's built-in hosting, database, and authentication services or choose external infrastructure.


## **5. Replit**


Replit provides a cloud development environment with AI-powered app building through Replit Agent, including native iOS app development using Expo and guided App Store submission. The platform supports multiple programming languages and frameworks.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full IDE in browser** : Terminal, package management, and collaborative editing.
- **Replit Agent** : AI-powered app generation, editing, and development assistance.
- **Deployment** : Host applications directly from the development environment.
- **Multiplayer collaboration** : Real-time coding with team members.


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit provides a complete development environment accessible through the browser. The platform includes Replit Agent for AI-assisted development and supports a wide range of programming languages and frameworks. Teams can build, test, and deploy applications within a single environment.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit bridges the gap between no-code and traditional development. Teams with some technical background who want flexibility and control may find the platform appealing. The platform also offers built-in database and authentication services alongside its development and deployment tools.


## **6. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow generates native mobile applications using the Flutter framework. The platform emphasizes code export and cross-platform development.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Native mobile apps** : Generate iOS and Android applications from one codebase.
- **Flutter framework:** Export standard Flutter code on paid plans for continued development.
- **Visual design** : Build interfaces through a component-based visual editor.
- **Firebase integration** : Connect to Google's backend services.


### **App Building Considerations**


FlutterFlow generates applications using the Flutter framework, allowing teams to build for iOS and Android from a single codebase. The platform provides a visual interface for designing app screens and defining logic. Teams can export Flutter code for continued development outside the platform.


### **Organizational Fit**


FlutterFlow targets teams specifically building mobile applications who want the option to export and customize Flutter code. The platform requires learning its visual interface and understanding Flutter conventions for advanced customization.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users create, refine, and publish websites and lightweight web apps directly through ChatGPT, subject to availability and workspace permissions. It offers a conversational approach to building hosted experiences without setting up a separate deployment workflow.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational website creation** : Describe and refine websites or lightweight apps through ChatGPT.
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish and share sites without arranging separate hosting.
- **Interactive applications** : Build dashboards, trackers, and other web experiences with supported data storage and sign-in features.
- **Sharing controls** : Manage access to published sites based on available plan and workspace permissions.


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites enables website and lightweight web application creation directly within ChatGPT conversations. The platform provides built-in hosting and publishing without requiring external deployment tools. Teams can build interactive web experiences with data storage and user sign-in features.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits users building websites, internal tools, and lightweight web applications within ChatGPT. Teams should evaluate its supported runtime, usage limits, and backend requirements before choosing it for more complex applications. For users who need managed full-stack infrastructure alongside existing AI assistants, plus iOS and Android app-building and publishing workflows, Floot offers a different approach.


## **Why Floot Stands Out as an Adalo Alternative**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) helps non-technical founders, freelancers, and businesses build full-stack applications through familiar AI assistants. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations for creating, editing, testing, and publishing applications, depending on connector permissions. Floot provides[managed backend infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , including PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, email, scheduled tasks, and hosting.


Floot uses existing AI subscriptions for connector-based development without charging for a second AI model. Users retain ownership of their code and data, with[full project exports](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) available on paid plans. The platform also supports[iOS and Android apps](https://floot.com/en/mobile) , with publishing subject to plan requirements, developer accounts, and app-store approval.


Floot's[Pro plan](https://floot.com/en/pricing) costs $25/month and includes 1,000 daily building actions and a $10 monthly hosting allowance, with additional usage deducted from prepaid hosting credits. Automatic top-ups are optional. It suits freelancers, agencies, and founders managing applications that require authentication, persistent data, and reliable hosting. Explore the[community showcase](https://floot.com/en/showcase) to see applications built with Floot.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What are the main differences between Adalo and AI-driven app builders like Floot?**


Adalo uses a visual drag-and-drop interface where teams assemble screens from pre-built components and define logic through its workflow system. Floot takes a conversational approach through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , allowing supported AI assistants to develop TypeScript/React applications backed by managed infrastructure. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions. The visual approach requires learning a specific interface, while the conversational approach lets teams iterate by describing changes in natural language.


### **Can teams use existing AI assistants to build apps with Floot, and what are the cost implications?**


Floot connects to supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, through the Model Context Protocol. This allows teams to use existing AI subscriptions, with connector development metered in Floot build actions rather than AI credits. Image generation and optional Floot AI features consume separate credits. Floot is free to start, while[Pro pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) begins at $25/month with 1,000 daily build actions and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. AI subscription costs, hosting overages, and optional Floot AI features remain separate.


### **How does Floot's managed infrastructure compare to what other Adalo alternatives offer?**


Floot includes managed Postgres databases, user authentication with Google/Microsoft OAuth brokering, file storage, transactional email, push notifications, and scheduled background tasks on published apps with a paid plan. Sending email to customers requires a verified sending domain on a paid Floot plan. Some alternatives require connecting external services like Supabase for databases or Resend for email. Floot's approach reduces core infrastructure setup, although third-party integrations may still require separate service accounts. The platform's[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) provide the essential backend components for working applications.


### **What kind of apps can teams build with Adalo alternatives, and are they suitable for mobile?**


Adalo alternatives support a range of applications from landing pages to full SaaS products with user accounts, payments, and complex data relationships. For mobile, approaches vary. Floot converts web apps to native iOS/Android shells, FlutterFlow generates Flutter code, Lovable focuses primarily on web applications, and Bolt.new supports both web and mobile development through Expo. Floot's free plan includes 2 mobile builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power includes unlimited builds. App-store publishing still requires developer accounts and store approval.


### **Is it possible to integrate custom code or third-party services with these app-building platforms?**


Floot projects use TypeScript and React, allowing direct code customization. The platform supports[third-party integrations](https://floot.com/en/integrations) with services such as Stripe, PayPal, Google Analytics, Zapier, and Twilio through APIs, with third-party accounts and credentials where required. Users own their code and data on every Floot plan, while full project ZIP export requires a paid plan. Bubble offers extensive plugins, Lovable supports code export for external development, and Replit provides a full development environment for integrations.
